observations.value: Opacity is central, blending with cardiac silhouette and mediastinum; not clearly separate from heart—consistent with pericardial effusion rather than a discrete herniated viscus

Smooth, broad-based, non-lobulated borders that merge with the heart—typical of pericardial effusion; diaphragmatic hernia usually shows sharper or irregular interface with lung and may displace adjacent structures
Homogeneous soft-tissue density without air-fluid level—argues against gastric herniation (which typically shows air or air-fluid level); pericardial effusion is uniformly fluid-density
Diaphragm obscured/elevated inferiorly but no clear hernia sac or displaced gastric bubble visible; absence of gastric air in right lower thorax undermines Y
Hernia probability very low (0.022), while Cardiomegaly high (0.676) and Mass moderate (0.49)—but mass likely reflects enlarged cardiac silhouette, not discrete lesion
Expert explicitly identifies opacity as 'Cardiac silhouette, mediastinum', not a separate structure like hernia
No pleural effusion detected—rules out pleural cause but does not distinguish between pericardial vs. diaphragmatic origin
Report states 'markedly enlarged heart' and 'no focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax'; supports cardiomegaly/pericardial effusion over hernia

Tool returned a bounding box for 'Diaphragmatic hernia', but this conflicts with visual evidence (no air, no gastric bubble, smooth cardiac-contiguous opacity) and other tools; likely false positive due to model overinterpretation
